summary.text: The Southern Oscillation is the atmospheric side of the El Niño–Southern Oscillation, a seesaw in surface air pressure between the tropical eastern and western Pacific.
It is coupled with changes in Pacific sea surface temperature, and wind, surface air pressure and cloudiness all respond to it.
Its negative phase, during El Niño, brings abnormally high pressure over Indonesia and low pressure over the East Pacific, and its positive phase during La Niña is the reverse.

facts.label: What swings
facts.value: Surface air pressure across the tropical Pacific

facts.label: Negative phase
facts.value: High pressure over Indonesia, during El Niño

facts.label: Positive phase
facts.value: The opposite pattern, during La Niña

facts.label: Cycle length
facts.value: Roughly every two to seven years, irregularly

items.prompt: Air pressure over Indonesia is abnormally high while it is abnormally low over the eastern Pacific. Which episode is under way?

options.label: El Niño
La Niña
Neutral
Both at once

items.explain: High pressure over Indonesia and the West Pacific with low pressure over the East Pacific is the negative phase, which occurs during El Niño episodes.

items.prompt: If you tracked the Southern Oscillation with instruments, what would you mainly be measuring swing back and forth?

options.label: Sea level between the Atlantic and Pacific
Rainfall over the coast of Antarctica
Surface air pressure across the tropical Pacific
Salt content of the ocean near Peru

items.explain: The Southern Oscillation is the oscillation in surface air pressure between the tropical eastern and western Pacific.

items.prompt: Weaker trade winds let warm water surge east, and the warmer sea then weakens the winds even more. What does this loop show?

options.label: The ocean does not respond to the winds
Ocean and atmosphere drive each other
Only the sun controls the trade winds
Winds change the sea but never the reverse

items.explain: In the Bjerknes feedback, atmospheric changes alter sea temperatures, which in turn alter the winds, so the air and sea are coupled.

items.prompt: During a swing of the oscillation, which changes would a weather station in the tropical Pacific pick up?

options.label: Tides only, with nothing changing in the air
Day length and the sun's energy output
Air pressure only, with no other changes
Shifts in wind, air pressure and cloud cover

items.explain: Numerous atmospheric features respond to the oscillation, including wind, surface air pressure and cloudiness.

items.prompt: Roughly how often does the system switch between El Niño, La Niña and neutral states?

options.label: Every year, like the seasons
Every 50 to 70 years
Every two to seven years
Exactly every eleven years

items.explain: The switching follows an irregular pattern but cycles about every two to seven years, with varying intensity.

items.prompt: As the world warms, what is happening to the droughts and floods linked to this oscillation?

options.label: Climate change makes them disappear
Climate change makes their effects worse
Climate change has no bearing on them
Climate change moves them to the Atlantic

items.explain: Although future trends in ENSO are uncertain, climate change exacerbates the effects of the droughts and floods associated with it.
